adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable.test.tsx 'Should render Edit/Delete button' tests mock hooks the component does not use (useAlertRuleAbility, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) while leaving useRulerRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbility at falsy defaults, so canEditRule/canDeleteRule are false and the positive-path find() assertions fail

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows changes to the tests’ mocks, not the RulesTable component’s internal hook usage. In RulesTable.test.tsx the suite now provides default mocks for all related hooks (useAlertRuleAbility, useRulerRuleAbility, useGrafanaPromRuleAbility, useRulerRuleAbilities, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) and individual tests override some of them. The finding asserts the component does not use the mocked hooks and instead depends on un-overridden defaults, but that hook usage cannot be verified from this diff and is contradicted by the test’s own inline comments about which hooks are used by which components.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable.test.tsx cloud rule tests assume only useRulerRuleAbilities needs mocking, but RuleActionsButtons calls singular useRulerRuleAbility which stays at the [false, false] default, causing cloud positive tests to render no buttons and fail

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the test scaffolding explicitly documents and mocks that **`RuleActionsButtons` uses `useAlertRuleAbility` (singular)**, while **`AlertRuleMenu` uses `useRulerRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (plural)**. The cloud-rule test cases in the diff only rely on `useAlertRuleAbility` for the action buttons and additionally mock `useRulerRuleAbilities` for the menu; there’s no diff evidence that `RulesTable`’s action buttons call `useRulerRuleAbility`. The only place in this diff where an actions component calls `useRulerRuleAbility` is `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, which is part of the rule-list UI, not `RulesTable` per the test comments. بنابراین the finding misreads the diff’s actual hook usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAbilities.ts useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities references symbols (useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport, useCanSilenceInFolder, ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata, useFolder, folderUid on GrafanaPromRuleDTO) not established in the diff, risking compile failure; also isPluginProvidedRule (RulerRuleDTO-typed guard) is fed a GrafanaPromRuleDTO

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, the newly added `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` uses `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(...)` but no `ctx` is defined in that function (and it cannot be defined at module scope via a hook), which would cause a compile/runtime failure. The finding’s mention of `folderUid` not existing is not supported by the diff (it already exists on `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase`), but the undefined `ctx` reference is a real, diff-grounded defect. The other referenced symbols (`useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport`, `useCanSilenceInFolder`) are not shown as imported/defined in this diff, but that is less strictly verifiable without full file context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx imports grantUserPermissions from '../mocks' and setFolderAccessControl from '../mocks/server/configure' which are not shown to be exported, risking import-time failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx changed imports to `grantUserPermissions` (from `../mocks`) and `setFolderAccessControl` (from `../mocks/server/configure`), but it does not include the source files for those modules, so the claim that they are “not shown to be exported” cannot be verified from this PR diff alone. The alleged import-time failure is therefore speculative based on missing context, not a demonstrable defect in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx: getEditableIdentifier only handles grafana promRule, so a cloud-ruled promRule passed without rule (allowed by union/RequireAtLeastOne type) triggers logWarning and returns null, silently dropping all action buttons for that row

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, Props now allows passing only promRule (RequireAtLeastOne with optional rule/promRule). getEditableIdentifier() can only construct an identifier from a RulerRuleDTO, or from a Grafana prom rule (prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)); otherwise it logs a warning and returns undefined, and the component returns null (dropping all action buttons). This is a real edge-case/API-footgun introduced by the diff, but the diff does not show any actual caller passing a non-Grafana promRule without a ruler rule, so a concrete broken behavior cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities wrapper hardcodes isFederated=false, so callers with federated (Mimir) rule groups now incorrectly get Edit/Delete/Pause affordances, and Delete on a federated rule makes a failing ruler call

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, the deprecated `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` wrapper now delegates to the new `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. The new `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` explicitly sets `isFederated = false` (with a TODO) and no longer calls `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)` (the import was removed). This means federated rule groups that were previously treated as immutable (no Edit/Delete/etc.) will now be treated as non-federated, potentially enabling Update/Delete/Pause UI affordances incorrectly. That’s a concrete behavioral regression visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rules that exist in the Ruler but not yet in Prometheus are silently dropped from the list; intermediate 'Creating'/'Deleting' states were removed with no replacement, and the tests verifying that behavior were deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes all logic that previously handled ruler/prom mismatch states. In `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, the `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` fetch, the `matchRules()` reconciliation, and rendering of "Creating" (ruler-only) and "Deleting" (prom-only via `RuleOperationListItem`) are deleted; the component now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)`, so any rule not present in the Prom response will not be shown. Correspondingly, `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` deletes the tests that asserted these creating/deleting behaviors (and removes `matchRules` tests entirely). Whether this is a bug depends on an external guarantee of strong consistency, which is not provable from the diff alone, but the behavioral regression described is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false with only a TODO, making federated rule groups appear mutable (Update/Delete/Pause buttons shown where actions will fail server-side) with no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` the diff replaces prior federated detection with a hardcoded `const isFederated = false;` (with a TODO) and still uses `immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided;`. This means federated ruler rule groups will no longer be marked immutable and will appear editable/removable (Update/Delete/Pause/Restore supported) when they previously could have been blocked. The diff also comments “TODO: Add support for federated rules” confirming the capability loss/regression; no tests are added to cover federated behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2 calls useRulerRuleAbility with rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined but the singular hook's signature change is not in this diff, risking a compile break or unverified semantics for undefined

adjudication.rationale: In `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, props now allow `rule?: RulerRuleDTO` (via `RequireAtLeastOne`), but the component still unconditionally calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />` without passing `rule`, so `rule` will be `undefined` at runtime/type level. In this diff, only `useRulerRuleAbilities` was updated to accept `RulerRuleDTO | undefined`; there is no shown corresponding change to the singular `useRulerRuleAbility` signature, so this introduces a likely TS compile error and/or undefined semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: createReturnTo() is dropped from the rule view href in GrafanaRuleListItem, losing return-to context (list page filter state) when users navigate back from the rule view

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit `createReturnTo()` handling that previously appended a `returnTo` query param to the rule view link. In the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, `GrafanaRuleListItem` built `href` as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`. In the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, `href` is now `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` context passed. This is a concrete behavior change that can break navigation back to the filtered list state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New menu test only asserts the fully-permissioned happy path; no negative test verifies menu items are hidden when permissions are denied, leaving the new ruler/prom ability OR-logic untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new GrafanaGroupLoader menu coverage that only checks the positive case: in `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, permissions are granted in `beforeEach`, and the test `should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked` asserts the menu items (silence/copy link/duplicate/export) are present and counts them. There is a negative RBAC test added only for the Edit button (`should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions`), but no test denies specific permissions (e.g., `AlertingRuleCreate`, `AlertingRuleRead`, `AlertingSilenceCreate`) and verifies the corresponding menu items are hidden. Given the new OR-logic in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` combining ruler and prom abilities (`canX = (rulerSupported&&allowed) || (grafanaSupported&&allowed)`), the absence of negative tests for menu items leaves that permission-gating/OR-logic behavior insufficiently exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities Silence ability composes silenceSupported with canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule without preserving old useCanSilence semantics, and no test covers folderless or recording-rule silence permissions

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new Silence ability logic for GrafanaPromRuleDTO in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`: `[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` instead of reusing the prior `useCanSilence(rule)` tuple used in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`. This is a meaningful behavioral/authorization composition change, but the diff alone does not prove it is incorrect because `useCanSilence` semantics are not shown. However, the added/updated tests (e.g. `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`) only cover the happy-path menu rendering with permissions and do not cover edge cases implied by the new logic such as `rule?.folderUid` being undefined (folderless) or non-alerting (recording) rules where `isAlertingRule` gates silencing. That lack of coverage is a concrete review issue tied to the new code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deletion of matchRules, RuleOperation.Creating, and RuleOperationListItem/RuleOperation.Deleting machinery removes eventual-consistency UI states, so newly created rules don't appear until propagation and just-deleted rules render as functional rows until Prometheus catches up

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the dual-source reconciliation in `GrafanaGroupLoader` (it no longer queries the Ruler API and no longer runs `matchRules`), and also deletes rendering of transitional UI via `RuleOperationListItem` with `RuleOperation.Deleting` and the `RuleOperation.Creating` path for ruler-only rules. Now the loader renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` as normal `GrafanaRuleListItem` rows. This definitely eliminates the explicit “creating/deleting” eventual-consistency UI handling; whether that becomes a user-visible defect depends on an assumption (strong consistency between Ruler and Prometheus) that is not proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The three matchRules unit tests covering propagation-lag behavior were deleted rather than ported

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the three `matchRules` unit tests were removed (the entire `describe('matchRules', ...)` block in `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` is deleted) and the `matchRules` helper itself is removed from `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`. Since the propagation-lag matching behavior is no longer present in the code, there is nothing to “port” those tests to; the finding implies an obligation that isn’t supported by the new implementation shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllAlertRuleAbilities rewritten to delegate to useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes const isFederated = false, causing all consumers passing full CombinedRule to treat federated rule groups as mutable (immutableRule gate no longer fires)

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` was changed to build a `groupIdentifierV2` and delegate to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. In the refactored `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, the federated check is explicitly disabled: `// TODO: Add support for federated rules ... const isFederated = false;` whereas previously `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);` and included it in `immutableRule`. This diff therefore removes the federated immutability gate for consumers calling `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` with a full `CombinedRule`, making federated rule groups no longer treated as immutable (mutable abilities may be granted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: returnTo parameter dropped from rule link in GrafanaRuleListItem, so clicking a rule and pressing Back no longer returns to filtered list state

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the previous implementation (deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) built the rule link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, preserving list state via a `returnTo` query param. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds the link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`, so navigation can no longer carry the return location/filter state. This is a concrete behavioral regression introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FilterView renders GrafanaRuleListItem on raw filter results with no error/loading handling, so missing/unfetchable rules render nothing silently, leaving 'Cannot load rule details' i18n keys orphaned

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces `GrafanaRuleLoader` (which did per-item fetching and showed loading/error Alerts using the removed i18n keys) with `GrafanaRuleListItem` that renders from an already-present `rule` object (`FilterView.tsx` now passes `rule={rule}`). There is no evidence in this diff that rules are “missing/unfetchable” at this point, since no fetch is attempted here anymore. Also, the finding claims the ‘Cannot load rule details’ i18n keys are left orphaned, but the diff explicitly deletes those keys from `public/locales/en-US/grafana.json`, so they are not orphaned by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stray // duplicate marker plus pre-existing copy in useIsRuleEditable creates a second hand-maintained parallel implementation of folder-permission evaluation that must be updated in both places to keep RBAC behavior consistent

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new folder-permission evaluation path specifically for GrafanaPromRuleDTO via the new internal hook `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` in `useAbilities.ts`, and it’s explicitly marked with a `// duplicate` comment at the call site (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` calls it: `... = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate`). This creates a second, parallel implementation of edit/remove RBAC evaluation (using `useFolder()` + `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(...)` + `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`) alongside the existing `useIsRuleEditable(...)` path used for `RulerRuleDTO`. That duplication is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue grounded in the diff (risk of divergence), but it is not a directly verifiable functional bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated-rule immutability guard deleted not migrated: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false with TODO, so federated rules are now reported as fully mutable allowing Edit/Delete on rules the old contract forbade

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` now hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO, whereas the prior logic (shown in the removed `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` body) used `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)` to make federated rules immutable. Because `immutableRule` feeds `Update`/`Delete`/`Pause`/`Restore` support via `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable`, federated rules will now be treated as mutable and can incorrectly show Edit/Delete capabilities.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization is now the OR of two parallel ability evaluators (ruler and prom paths) so the most permissive path always wins; should pick one evaluator based on rule origin instead of unioning both

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly unions (ORs) permissions from two different ability evaluators. In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport` are computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` using `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)`. Similarly in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, `canEditRule` is the OR of `useRulerRuleAbility(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...)`. This means if either evaluator returns a permissive result (due to differing logic, data staleness, or mismatched rule representation), the UI will enable actions. The review comment that it may be safer to select a single evaluator based on rule origin/type (instead of unioning) is a concrete, diff-grounded design/security concern, though the diff doesn’t prove it causes an actual incorrect authorization in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stated goal of removing ruler API requests in list view not implemented: useRulerRuleAbilities is called unconditionally alongside useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, doubling request fan-out per rule row across N rows

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx, the component now always calls both useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, [...]) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., [...]) on every render, then ORs their results (e.g., canPause/canDelete/etc.). There is no conditional gating to avoid running the ruler-based abilities when the consumer is the list view (where ruler API requests were removed). While the diff alone doesn’t prove these hooks trigger ruler API network calls, it does show the redundant dual ability-check path being executed unconditionally, which could undermine the stated goal via extra work/request fan-out.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ModifyExport support narrowed from isGrafanaManagedAlertRule to isAlertingRule, silently removing Export for Grafana-managed recording rules

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes ModifyExport support logic for Grafana Prom rules: in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport` is now gated by `isAlertingRule` (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`) rather than by “Grafana-managed rule” generally (previously `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` used `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` and then `[isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, exportAllowed]`). Since Grafana-managed recording rules satisfy `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` but not `...alertingRule(rule)`, this change removes export support for recording rules, which will hide/disable Export in menus that depend on `AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silence permission semantics changed from alertmanager-aware (useCanSilence) to folder-permission-only (canSilenceInFolder), silently granting conditions the old check enforced

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the Silence ability logic changes from the previous `useCanSilence(rule)` approach used for ruler rules to a new condition: `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` (see `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`). This is a real, diff-grounded semantic change in how silence eligibility is computed for `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`. However, the finding’s claim that it became “folder-permission-only” is not fully supported by the diff because the new logic also gates on `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` and `isAlertingRule`. Without the implementations of `useCanSilence`, `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport`, and `useCanSilenceInFolder` in the diff, we can’t verify that alertmanager-aware constraints were removed or that this silently grants extra access—only that the logic is different and warrants review/confirmation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: For a datasource (Mimir/cloud) rule passed as promRule only, getEditableIdentifier returns undefined and the row renders with no action buttons; RequireAtLeastOne type signature invites this silently broken call shape

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2 the props were widened to `RequireAtLeastOne<{ rule?: RulerRuleDTO; promRule?: Rule }>` and the component now returns `null` when `getEditableIdentifier(...)` returns `undefined`. `getEditableIdentifier` only constructs an identifier from a `rule` (ruler rule) or from a *Grafana* prom rule (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)`); any non-Grafana `promRule` passed without `rule` will hit the logWarning path and yield `undefined`, resulting in no action buttons. The diff does not show an actual call site passing a datasource/cloud promRule-only today, so the “row renders with no action buttons” part isn’t directly verifiable, but the new type/API shape does allow this silently broken combination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rules in transitional states vanish from the list instead of rendering Creating/Deleting placeholders in GrafanaGroupLoader rewrite; the corresponding tests and behavior were removed together

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites `GrafanaGroupLoader` to only query Prometheus (`useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`) and render `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules`, removing the Ruler query and the `matchRules` logic that previously rendered placeholders for transitional states: ruler-only rules as `RuleOperation.Creating` and prom-only rules as `RuleOperationListItem` with `RuleOperation.Deleting`. With this change, a ruler-only rule would not be rendered at all (it would “vanish”), and prom-only rules would no longer show a deleting placeholder. However, the diff also includes commentary implying Grafana Prom rules are now strongly consistent, so this may be an intentional scope change rather than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaRuleListItem still accepts an operation prop that no caller passes - dead API confirming the state was dropped

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `GrafanaRuleListItem` declares an optional `operation?: RuleOperation` prop (new file `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`) and current callers in this diff (`FilterView.tsx`, `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`) do not pass it. However, this is not a verifiable defect; it's simply an unused optional API surface/leftover parameter. The claim that it 'confirms the state was dropped' is interpretive and not grounded as a bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: showLocation defaults to true but GrafanaGroupLoader needs false and FilterView passes true explicitly; default contradicts call sites' purpose and next consumer who forgets gets redundant location column

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `GrafanaRuleListItem` has `showLocation = true` by default, but the two shown call sites both pass the intended value explicitly: `GrafanaGroupLoader` sets `showLocation={false}` (to avoid redundant location in the folder>group hierarchy) and `FilterView` sets `showLocation={true}`. So there’s no verifiable defect or contradiction in current behavior introduced by this PR; the concern about a future consumer “forgetting” is speculative and not evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaRuleListItem drops returnTo from the view href so navigation from the list loses return context the previous UX preserved

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `returnTo` parameter that was previously included in the Grafana rule view link. Deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` built `href` as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` now sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`, so list-to-view navigation can no longer preserve return context as it did before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities wrapper keeps CombinedRule-shaped signature but silently changes output for federated rules - internal semantic break behind unchanged public shape with no warning

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` is kept with the same CombinedRule-shaped signature but is changed to simply `return useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. Inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, federated handling is explicitly removed: `// TODO: Add support for federated rules` and `const isFederated = false;` replacing the previous `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);`. This silently changes abilities for federated rule groups (they may become editable/removable when they previously were treated as immutable), while the wrapper’s public shape remains the same (only marked `@deprecated` without warning about changed semantics).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rules pending creation (Ruler-only) or deletion (Prometheus-only) are no longer rendered in GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx, so a just-created rule vanishes until Prometheus propagates it and a just-deleted rule persists with full action buttons

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes all Ruler-side fetching and reconciliation in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, `matchRules`, the “Creating” rendering for Ruler-only rules, and the “Deleting” `RuleOperationListItem` for Prometheus-only rules are all deleted. The loader now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` as normal `GrafanaRuleListItem`s with action buttons. This makes the finding accurate that transitional Ruler-only / Prom-only states are no longer explicitly represented; whether that is a true defect depends on the (not diff-proven) assumption of strong consistency between Ruler and Prometheus.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests pinning the Creating/Deleting transitional behavior and matchRules unit tests were deleted and replaced with menu-button smoke tests, silently changing acceptance criteria and making the regression unobservable

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the transitional-state logic and its associated tests: `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` no longer queries the Ruler API, deletes `matchRules(...)`, stops rendering ruler-only rules as `RuleOperation.Creating`, and removes the `promOnlyRules`/`RuleOperationListItem` path that showed `RuleOperation.Deleting`. Correspondingly, `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` deletes the unit tests that pinned those Creating/Deleting behaviors and the `matchRules` unit-test suite, replacing them with broader “More button/menu items” smoke tests. This is a concrete, reviewable change in tested acceptance criteria that makes regressions in those transitional/mismatch scenarios unobservable (even if the product intent is to rely on strong consistency).

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllAlertRuleAbilities was gutted into a shim calling useAllRulerRuleAbilities which hardcodes isFederated = false, so federated rule groups incorrectly get Edit/Delete actions instead of being read-only

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` is changed into a shim that calls `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, and inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` the federated check is explicitly removed and replaced with `const isFederated = false;` (with a TODO). Previously, the code used `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` as part of `immutableRule` to prevent edit/delete for federated rule groups. With `isFederated` hardcoded to false, federated rules will no longer be treated as immutable and can incorrectly receive Update/Delete abilities when `useIsRuleEditable` returns editable/removable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx drops returnTo from the rule view URL, causing users to lose list filter/search context when navigating back from the view

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous `returnTo` query param when building the Grafana rule view link. The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`/`GrafanaRuleListItem` computed `const returnTo = createReturnTo();` and used `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, while the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` uses `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`. This is a concrete behavior change that can break preserving list context when navigating back from the rule view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getEditableIdentifier returns undefined and the RuleActionsButtons.V2 component renders no buttons for any prom rule that is not Grafana-managed, hiding contract violations behind a logWarning instead of failing loudly

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2, getEditableIdentifier() returns undefined for non-Grafana prom rules (only handles `rule` or `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)`), logs a warning, and the component then returns null (`if (!identifier) return null;`). This does indeed silently drop all action buttons in that case, which can mask an unexpected usage/contract violation behind `logWarning` rather than surfacing an error. The diff does not show this happening for current Grafana list usage (GrafanaRuleListItem passes a GrafanaPromRuleDTO), so it’s more of a robustness/contract concern than a proven functional defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The !promResponse branch in GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx conflates query errors with 'no rule groups found', showing the informational alert instead of an error state when the prom query fails

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx the new implementation only checks `isPromResponseLoading` and then `if (!promResponse) { return <Alert ... /> }`, but it no longer inspects the query `error` result from `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`. When the Prom query fails, RTK Query typically yields `data`/`promResponse` as undefined while `error` is set, so this branch will be taken and the component will render the same “cannot load”/informational alert as for other “no data” cases, instead of a distinct error state. This is a behavior regression introduced by removing the previous ruler+prom error handling and not replacing it for prom errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu.tsx permission check and acted-on rule object can diverge: canDelete etc. OR ruler-rule and prom-rule abilities while getEditableIdentifier independently picks the action target, with no uid cross-check between rulerRule and promRule, allowing the menu to gate on rule A's permissions while acting on rule B's uid

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ability gating is now computed as an OR across two different rule representations (AlertRuleMenu.tsx combines useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, ...) with useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule ...), and RuleActionsButtons.V2 combines useRulerRuleAbility(rule, ...) with useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(promRule ...)). Separately, the acted-on target identifier is chosen independently in getEditableIdentifier(): it uses the RulerRuleDTO identifier if `rule` is present, otherwise uses the GrafanaPromRuleDTO uid. There is no explicit invariant check that `rulerRule` and `promRule` refer to the same underlying rule/uid when both are provided, so the codebase now has a concrete, diff-grounded risk of permission checks being satisfied via one object while the action target (edit URL / menu actions) is derived from the other. The diff does not prove such mismatched inputs can occur in practice, but the lack of cross-check is real and introduced/exposed by the new dual-ability logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities in useAbilities.ts uses globally-scoped rulesPermissions.create for Duplicate while sibling checks (update/delete) are folder-scoped, producing inconsistent authorization UI for users with folder-scoped RBAC denies

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `Duplicate` is computed as `toAbility(duplicateSupported, rulesPermissions.create)` where `rulesPermissions` comes from `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`, i.e. a plain permission check without folder metadata. Meanwhile edit/delete are explicitly folder-scoped via `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` using `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(..., folder)`, and silence is folder-scoped via `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)`. This inconsistency can make the UI show Duplicate as allowed based on a global create permission even when folder-scoped RBAC would deny creating/duplicating in that folder (leading to incorrect/failed actions).

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable.test.tsx auto-mocks the entire useAbilities module, so the new OR-combination logic for canDelete is never executed with real code and its correctness (vs dead code, inverted, or wrong short-circuit) cannot be verified

adjudication.rationale: While RulesTable.test.tsx does `jest.mock('../../hooks/useAbilities')`, that only replaces the hook implementations. The new OR-combination logic for `canDelete` (and others) is in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` itself (e.g. `const canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed);`) and will still execute when the component renders, using the mocked hook return values as inputs. So it’s not true that the OR logic is “never executed”; what’s not exercised is the real ability-hook internals, which is a different claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable tests mock ruler-based and prom-based abilities to identical values, so there is no test case with divergent mock values for the scenario the OR semantics exists for (ruler denies but prom allows or vice versa)

adjudication.rationale: The updated `RulesTable.test.tsx` does include divergent mock values between ruler-based and prom-based ability hooks. In `beforeEach`, plural hooks default to `[false, false]` for all actions, and individual Grafana-rule tests override only `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (or prom singular) while leaving ruler hooks at the default `false`, exercising the OR path in `AlertRuleMenu` (e.g., ruler denies/unsupported but prom allows). Cloud-rule tests override `useRulerRuleAbilities` while prom abilities are effectively skipped via `skipToken`. So the claim that ruler/prom are mocked to identical values with no divergent case is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The auto-mocked module makes skipToken an auto-mock artifact, so the prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken guard in the component is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `jest.mock('../../hooks/useAbilities')`, which would auto-mock exports from that module, potentially including `skipToken`. However, the finding’s conclusion (“so the `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken` guard in the component is never exercised”) is not verifiable from the diff: that guard is in the component and will still execute based on `promRule`’s type, regardless of how `skipToken` is mocked, and the tests include both Grafana and Cloud rules where the else-path could be taken. Also, in the tests where the module is mocked, the hooks that would interpret `skipToken` (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`) are themselves mocked, so `skipToken` identity semantics are not relevant there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' test bakes in the absence of the Delete menu item instead of asserting it: assertions enumerate silence, copyLink, duplicate, export but not delete, and hard-codes expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4), so a broken delete wiring would pass unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, the test "should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked" explicitly asserts the presence of Silence, Copy link, Duplicate, and Export, and then hard-codes `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)`. It defines a `delete` selector in `ui.menuItems` and grants delete permissions in `beforeEach`, but never asserts the Delete menu item. As written, the test would still pass if Delete were accidentally not rendered/wired, so it leaves a specific permission-driven action unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The ui.menuItems.delete() selector is defined in the ui object of GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx but never used in assertions

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, the ui.menuItems.delete selector is indeed defined in the ui object (under menuItems) but no test assertion references ui.menuItems.delete(); the assertions only check silence/copyLink/duplicate/export. However, this is just an unused test helper/dead code nit and not a verifiable defect or substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAbilities.ts useAllAlertRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated = false, a behavioral regression that silently makes federated rule groups editable/deletable (gating Delete, Update, DeletePermanently, Restore, Pause), with zero test coverage anywhere in the diff for federated rule immutability

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` now hard-codes `isFederated = false` (with a TODO) and removes prior federated detection (`isFederatedRuleGroup` import removed and the old code path `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);` is gone). Since `immutableRule` is computed as `isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`, this change makes federated rules no longer treated as immutable, thereby enabling Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently when they should be blocked. The new/modified tests in the diff cover Grafana/cloud RBAC and menu items, but none assert federated immutability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable.test.tsx Edit/Delete permission tests use redundant identical mock implementations for useAlertRuleAbility and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, making them unable to detect a regression where the component drops one hook input entirely; tests should mock divergent values per hook and assert the button reflects the OR

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the Grafana-rule permission tests often set `useAlertRuleAbility` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` to return the same supported/allowed tuples for the relevant action (e.g., Update/Delete returning `[true,false]` while others are `[true,true]`). Since the production code now combines abilities with an OR across sources (e.g. in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` it computes `canDelete = (ruler...) || (grafana...)`), using identical mock behavior per hook makes the tests unable to catch a regression where one hook is no longer consulted (dropping one side of the OR). This is a real, diff-grounded test-coverage weakness, not a functional defect in the shipped code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New GrafanaRuleListItem/GrafanaGroupLoader path drops the ruler-rule join, so rules still propagating (previously shown as 'Creating') or stale prom-only rules (previously shown as 'Deleting') no longer render in the UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably removes the ruler API fetch and the prom↔ruler reconciliation logic that previously surfaced transitional states. In `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, the `matchRules` join, the “creating” path (ruler rule without matching prom rule), and the “deleting” `promOnlyRules` rendering via `RuleOperationListItem` are all deleted, and the component now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules`. This means the UI no longer has code paths to show those interim Creating/Deleting list items if prom and ruler become temporarily inconsistent. Whether that inconsistency can still occur is not proven by the diff, so it’s not a strictly provable defect, but it is a concrete edge-case/behavior drop introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:65: ruler/prom reconciliation with 'Creating'/'Deleting' transient states was removed, so a rule created via ruler API but not yet propagated to Prometheus vanishes from the list with no skeleton, 'Creating' row, or warning log

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove ruler/prom reconciliation and the related transient UI: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx no longer queries the ruler API (useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery removed), no longer computes `matches`/`promOnlyRules`, and no longer renders `RuleOperation.Creating` / `RuleOperation.Deleting` rows or logs the warning from `matchRules` (entire function deleted). It now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules`. However, the finding’s core claim (that a ruler-created rule can exist without a Prometheus counterpart long enough to “vanish”) depends on runtime consistency guarantees not verifiable from the diff; the diff even previously commented Prom rules “should be strongly consistent now.” So the removal is real and actionable as an edge-case/behavior regression risk, but not provably a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAbilities.ts (useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable, if (!folder) branch): folder fetch failure or denial leaves folder undefined with loading false, hook returns a terminal error-free { isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false }, indistinguishable from RBAC denial, silently removing Edit/Delete buttons

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` which relies on `useFolder(folderUID)` and, in the `if (!folder)` branch, returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading }` with no separate error/unknown state. If `useFolder` yields `folder === undefined` while `loading === false` (e.g., folder lookup failed or access denied), the UI will treat the rule as non-editable/removable without any distinguishable signal from a true RBAC denial. This is grounded in the new hook logic shown; whether it’s a "bug" depends on expected UX/error handling, but it is a concrete edge-case/observability concern created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx (getEditableIdentifier): when invoked with only a non-Grafana promRule, component logs a warning and returns null, silently dropping all action buttons with no user-facing error or fallback UI

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, getEditableIdentifier() explicitly returns undefined (after logWarning) when only promRule is provided and it is not a Grafana prom rule (it only handles `rule` or `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)`). The component then does `if (!identifier) { return null; }`, which drops the entire actions UI with no user-facing fallback. The diff shows this behavior clearly; what’s not verifiable from the diff alone is whether such a non-Grafana `promRule` callsite actually occurs, so it’s best treated as an edge-case/design gap rather than a confirmed broken flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:65: new code never inspects the query's error field, so a failed useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery falls through to the 'couldn't find any rule groups' not-found Alert, reporting infrastructure failure as empty results

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, the `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery` result is destructured as `{ data: promResponse, isLoading: isPromResponseLoading }` with no `error` handling. After loading, the code does `if (!promResponse) { return <Alert .../>; }`, so a failed query (where RTK Query sets `error` and leaves `data` undefined) will be treated the same as “no response/empty” and show the generic not-found/cannot-load alert instead of surfacing the actual error state. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.
